name: Question 15
problem: Find the second derivative of $f(t)={e}^{3t+2}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j-2{t}^{5}\,k$ with respect to $t.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{3t+2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{t}^{5})\,k \\  & =3{e}^{3t+2}\,i+(-2\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j+(-2\cdot 5{t}^{4})\,k \\  & =3{e}^{3t+2}\,i-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j-10{t}^{4}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

  

Then, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{3t+2})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-10{t}^{4})\,k \\  & =3(3{e}^{3t+2})\,i-2(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)\,j-10(4{t}^{3})\,k \\  & =9{e}^{3t+2}\,i-4\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j-40{t}^{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Find the second derivative of f(t)=e3t+2i+cos⁡2tj−2t5k with respect to t.

a
9e3t+2i−4cos⁡2tj−40t3k
b
3e3t+2i+cos⁡2tj−10t3k
c
9e3t+2i−cos⁡2tj+20t3k
d
3e3t+2i+4cos⁡2tj−40t3k
e
e3t+2i−cos⁡2tj+20t3k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the derivative of f(t) by differentiating each component.

f′(t)=ddt(e3t+2)i+ddt(cos⁡2t)j+ddt(−2t5)k=3e3t+2i+(−2⋅sin⁡2t)j+(−2⋅5t4)k=3e3t+2i−2sin⁡2tj−10t4k

Then, we calculate f″(t) by differentiating f′(t):

f″(t)=ddt(3e3t+2)i+ddt(−2sin⁡2t)j+ddt(−10t4)k=3(3e3t+2)i−2(2cos⁡2t)j−10(4t3)k=9e3t+2i−4cos⁡2tj−40t3k
